dct_description_sm: The purpose of this project was to evaluate the use of non-invasively collected polar bear tissue samples for their use in a Polar Bear Activity Survey. This non-invasive survey was conducted on the ground using Inuit knowledge and labor. Once this evaluation is complete, robust and valid components of the survey will be integrated into a meaningful activity survey. This survey will provide an estimate of Minimum Number Known Alive (MNKA) for any polar bear population, and an estimate of their health and diet. The next step is to evaluate these components in terms of conducting more extensive polar bear census studies from which management data can be meaningfully derived. These developments should see Inuit participate in a more significant way in the monitoring and management of Nunavut's polar bears. Also this project will provide a more accurate estimate of MKNA for M'Clintock Channel polar bears. This information will be important in re-considering the near zero quota the residents of Gjoa Haven have endured for the last 10 years.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Economics
dct_title_s: Toward the optimization of an Inuit non-invasive polar bear survey: completing the evaluation of non-invasively collected polar bear tissue (NGMP ID EC26)
